task1.title: Numbers of four fish species worldwide, 1982–2007
task1.prompt: The chart below shows the number of four different species of fish between 1982 and 2007.

chartDesc.title: Kinds of fish worldwide
chartDesc.overview: Overall, Atlantic Cod decreased sharply over the period but remained the most numerous species in all years except around 1992, when Yellowfin Tuna peaked. Albacore Tuna remained consistently the lowest throughout the 25-year period with almost no overall change.
keyFeatures: Atlantic Cod started highest in 1982 at around 234,000, fell to about 132,000 by 2007.
Yellowfin Tuna rose from 150,000 in 1982 to a peak of around 190,000 in 1992, surpassing Atlantic Cod, before declining to 100,000 in 2007.
Haddock fluctuated slightly between approximately 74,000 and 84,000 throughout the period.
Albacore Tuna remained low and relatively stable, rising slightly from around 11,000 to 13,000.

task1.instruction: Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
task1.sampleBand8:
The line graph shows how the worldwide numbers of four fish species — Atlantic cod, haddock, yellowfin tuna and albacore tuna — changed between 1982 and 2007.

Overall, the two most numerous species, Atlantic cod and yellowfin tuna, both ended the period well below their starting levels, while haddock drifted down only slightly and albacore tuna, the smallest population, was the only species to grow at all.

Atlantic cod began as by far the most plentiful fish, at roughly 235,000, but its number fell steeply to about 152,000 in 1992, allowing yellowfin tuna — which had climbed from 150,000 to a peak of around 190,000 — to overtake it briefly. Thereafter the two species swapped places again: cod recovered modestly to about 165,000 in 2002 before slipping to 133,000, whereas yellowfin numbers fell continuously after 1992, ending at approximately 100,000, two-thirds of their original level.

The remaining species changed far less. Haddock stayed within a narrow band, easing from about 85,000 to 74,000 over the 25 years, while albacore tuna remained fairly constant at just over 10,000, inching up to around 13,000 by 2007 — still the rarest of the four by a wide margin.

Umuman olganda, eng ko'p sonli ikki tur — Atlantika treskasi va sariq qanotli tunets — davrni boshlang'ich darajalaridan ancha pastda yakunladi, pikshа soni esa atigi biroz pasayib bordi, eng kichik populyatsiya bo'lgan albakor tunets esa umuman o'sgan yagona tur bo'ldi.

Atlantika treskasi taxminan 235 000 bilan beqiyos darajada eng serob baliq sifatida boshlagan, biroq uning soni 1992-yilga kelib taxminan 152 000 gacha tik pasaydi va bu 150 000 dan qariyb 190 000 lik cho'qqiga ko'tarilgan sariq qanotli tunetsga uni qisqa muddatga ortda qoldirish imkonini berdi. Shundan so'ng ikki tur yana o'rin almashdi: treska 2002-yilda taxminan 165 000 gacha birmuncha tiklanib, keyin 133 000 ga tushdi, sariq qanotli tunets soni esa 1992-yildan keyin uzluksiz kamayib, taxminan 100 000 da — dastlabki darajasining uchdan ikki qismida — yakunlandi.

Qolgan turlar ancha kam o'zgardi. Piksha 25 yil davomida tor oraliqda qolib, taxminan 85 000 dan 74 000 gacha yengil pasaydi, albakor tunets esa 10 000 dan sal ko'proq darajada deyarli o'zgarmay turdi va 2007-yilga kelib taxminan 13 000 gacha sekin ko'tarildi — bu hali ham to'rttala tur ichida katta farq bilan eng kam uchraydigani edi.

task2.title: Should university education be free for all?
task2.prompt: Some people believe that people have the right to a university education and that the government should make it free, regardless of their financial background. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
task2.instruction: Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.
task2.sampleBand8:
Whether governments should make university education free for everyone, whatever their financial background, is a divisive question. I largely agree that higher education should be free at the point of use, although I believe the policy needs sensible limits.

The strongest argument for free universities is equality of opportunity. When degrees depend on the ability to pay, talented students from poor families are either excluded or saddled with debt for decades, which wastes ability the whole country needs. Societies also gain collectively from graduates: doctors, engineers and teachers repay the public investment many times over through higher tax revenues and better services, just as countries such as Germany and Norway, which charge no tuition fees, continue to prosper. In this sense, higher education is a public good comparable to schooling or healthcare, and access to it can reasonably be described as a right.

However, the objections deserve attention. Fully free provision is enormously expensive, and the money must come from taxpayers, many of whom never attended university; there is also a risk that students who pay nothing take their studies less seriously, or that quality falls as enrolment balloons. For these reasons, I would attach conditions: free places should be tied to satisfactory academic progress, and funding should prioritise socially valuable fields and students who genuinely could not otherwise afford to study, with means-tested support for living costs.

In conclusion, I agree that financial background should never decide who can attend university, and that government-funded, tuition-free education — subject to reasonable performance requirements — is the fairest and, in the long run, the most productive arrangement.
task2.uzSampleBand8:
Hukumatlar oliy ta'limni moddiy ahvolidan qat'i nazar hamma uchun bepul qilishi kerakmi degan savol fikrlarni ikkiga bo'ladi. Men oliy ta'lim foydalanish nuqtasida bepul bo'lishi kerak degan fikrga asosan qo'shilaman, garchi bu siyosatga oqilona chegaralar zarur deb hisoblasam-da.

Bepul universitetlar foydasiga eng kuchli dalil — imkoniyatlar tengligi. Diplom to'lov qobiliyatiga bog'liq bo'lganda, kambag'al oilalardan chiqqan iqtidorli talabalar yo chetda qoladi, yo o'nlab yillarga qarz yukini orttiradi — bu esa butun mamlakatga kerak bo'lgan iqtidorni isrof qiladi. Jamiyat ham bitiruvchilardan birgalikda yutadi: shifokorlar, muhandislar va o'qituvchilar yuqoriroq soliq tushumlari va yaxshiroq xizmatlar orqali davlat sarmoyasini necha barobar qilib qaytaradi — xuddi o'qish to'lovi olmaydigan Germaniya va Norvegiya kabi mamlakatlar farovon yashashda davom etayotgani kabi. Shu ma'noda oliy ta'lim maktab yoki tibbiyotga qiyoslanadigan ijtimoiy ne'mat bo'lib, unga kirish imkoniyatini haq deb atash o'rinli.

Biroq e'tirozlar ham e'tiborga loyiq. To'liq bepul ta'lim g'oyat qimmatga tushadi va mablag' soliq to'lovchilardan — ularning ko'pi hech qachon universitetda o'qimagan — kelishi kerak; hech narsa to'lamaydigan talabalar o'qishga yengilroq qarashi yoki qabul keskin shishib ketishi bilan sifat tushish xavfi ham bor. Shu sabablarga ko'ra men shartlar qo'ygan bo'lardim: bepul o'rinlar qoniqarli akademik natijaga bog'lanishi, mablag' esa ijtimoiy qimmatli yo'nalishlarga hamda o'qishga chindan ham qurbi yetmaydigan talabalarga, turmush xarajatlari uchun daromadga qarab beriladigan yordam bilan birga, ustuvor yo'naltirilishi kerak.

Xulosa qilib aytganda, moddiy ahvol kimning universitetda o'qishini hech qachon hal qilmasligi kerakligiga va davlat mablag'idagi, o'qish to'lovisiz ta'lim — oqilona natija talablariga bo'ysungan holda — eng adolatli va uzoq istiqbolda eng samarali tartib ekaniga qo'shilaman.
